title: Claude can now test your app like a real user

beats.purpose: Open with the main result in one strong line.
beats.voiceover: Claude can now test your app like a real user.
beats.onScreenText: Claude can now test your app like a real user.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Strong opening frame. Show Claude Code and a web app open in Chrome. Make it obvious that Claude is interacting with the app in the browser.
beats.notes: Keep it bold and clean. This is the promise.

beats.purpose: Show why manual testing is annoying and inefficient.
beats.voiceover: Manually clicking through your app after every change takes time, you still miss bugs, and honestly it gets annoying fast.
beats.onScreenText: Manual testing takes time. And you still miss things.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show the painful workflow: code change, open app, click through pages, fill inputs, miss something, go back, test again.
beats.notes: This should feel repetitive and frustrating.

beats.voiceover: Now Claude Code can connect directly to Chrome and do that testing for you.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show Claude Code connected to Chrome. Browser is open with a local app ready to be tested.
beats.notes: Simple reveal frame. Don't overload it.

beats.purpose: Introduce what Claude can do once Chrome is connected.
beats.voiceover: And that means Claude can actually use your app, not just write code for it.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Intro card for the capabilities section. Could show a small browser visual with multiple action markers or icons around it.
beats.notes: Acts like a mini chapter break before the list.

beats.purpose: Show the first group of practical actions.
beats.voiceover: It can click buttons, move through pages, and fill out forms for you.
beats.onScreenText:
Click buttons
Open pages
Fill forms
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show 3 quick action examples: button click, page navigation, form filling.
beats.notes: These should be very concrete. Good place for more energetic animation.

beats.purpose: Show the second group of practical actions.
beats.voiceover: It can also check validation, inspect browser errors, and show you exactly what happened on screen.
beats.onScreenText:
Check validation
Read errors
Show what happened
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show validation message, browser console error, and a visible test flow happening on screen.
beats.notes: This is the more technical half of the benefits.

beats.purpose: Quickly show how to connect Claude Code to Chrome.
beats.voiceover: To connect it, install the Claude Chrome extension, then start Claude Code with chrome enabled.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Quick setup sequence. Show the extension in Chrome and then terminal / Claude Code setup step.
beats.notes: Keep this fast. Enough to show the idea, not a full tutorial.

beats.purpose: Show the exact kind of prompt the viewer can use.
beats.voiceover: Then you can simply ask Claude to test your app, for example: test the signup flow and tell me what breaks.
beats.onScreenText:
Test the signup flow
and tell me what breaks.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Screen recording of Claude Code receiving a prompt to test the signup flow on the local app.
beats.notes: Make the prompt readable. This is the 'I can try this too' moment.

beats.purpose: Prove that the testing is happening live on screen.
beats.voiceover: Now you can watch Claude click through the app, test the flow, and inspect the result live on screen.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Show Claude actively using the app in Chrome: clicking, typing, submitting, and checking the result.
beats.notes: This should feel like the strongest visual proof moment.

beats.purpose: End with a clear next action for the viewer.
beats.voiceover: Follow for more AI app building tips.
beats.onScreenText: Follow for more AI app building tips.
beats.visualPlaceholder: Clean ending frame. Keep Claude Code and Chrome theme, with simple follow CTA.
